title: La Maternelle
summary: "La Maternelle" by Léon Frapié is a novel published in 1904 that won the Prix Goncourt. After losing her dowry and fiancé to family ruin, educated Rose is forced to work as an attendant at a Paris kindergarten serving 150 working-class children. Despite the menial tasks and desperate circumstances, she forms deep bonds with the neglected children who turn to her as a mother figure. The novel offers a critical portrait of poverty and public education's role in shaping obedience rather than liberation. (This is an automatically generated summary.)
